end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified local foods such as home-made roti and nearby spinach.
Compared foods by distance and selected the 10 km source over the 230 km source.
Explained that longer journeys use more fuel and can increase pollution.
Discussed refrigeration during transport and linked it with extra electricity use; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, identifying local foods, comparing travel distances, and linking longer journeys with fuel use and pollution. They clearly explained that nearby spinach or food from a nearby farmer travels less and needs less fuel. They also connected refrigerated transport with extra electricity use and pollution; no mix-up remained in the final responses. At home, ask them to choose two foods and trace which one likely travelled farther, then discuss fuel, pollution, and freshness.
